EQUIPMENT

Working Platforms: Put Ownership in the Contract, Not in an Assumption

Clarify who designs, provides, accepts and maintains the operating surface.

In this insight

Treat the platform as a defined work itemShare the correct plant informationPlan the ongoing interfaceKeep readiness evidence accessibleFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Treat the platform as a defined work item

A working platform supports the intended plant operations and requires a project-specific approach. It should not be reduced to an informal promise that the site will be level. The relevant specialists must establish the technical requirements. Procurement should make the design, construction, verification and maintenance responsibilities visible so no party assumes another has taken ownership.

Share the correct plant information

The platform designer needs appropriate information about the intended equipment and operations. The project team should coordinate that information and control changes. If the proposed plant or working arrangement changes, ask the responsible designer whether reassessment is required. A platform arrangement developed for one set of assumptions should not silently become the basis for a different operation.

Plan the ongoing interface

The platform can be affected by other site activities, excavations, services and changing access. Identify who controls work that could alter it and how the operating teams are informed. Maintenance and inspection arrangements should be part of the agreed scope. A handover at the start does not remove the need to manage the platform as the site evolves.

Keep readiness evidence accessible

Agree which documents and confirmations are needed before the intended operation begins. Retain the relevant drawings, acceptance records and change history in a location the responsible teams can use. International industry guidance can inform discussion, but the project’s applicable requirements and engineering decisions govern. The client’s practical contribution is to prevent a critical enabling item from falling between contracts.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Assign platform responsibilities explicitly.
  • Coordinate plant information with the designer.
  • Manage changes throughout the operating period.
